annotations.keyFindings: Same-day discharge failed in 21 percent of 2,940 procedures; age over 70, higher anaesthetic risk, a start after 13:00, rescue-treated nausea and a drain were associated with failure; a nine-predictor model reached a c statistic of 0.72 without validation.
annotations.limitations: Predictors partly selected by significance; missing data above 20 percent for some variables; no validation.

annotations.keyFindings: Failure was 38 percent for starts after 14:00 and 14 percent for starts before 11:00; list order was partly chosen by risk in one hospital.
annotations.limitations: Two hospitals; confounding by indication for list position.

annotations.keyFindings: Nausea severity was documented in 41 percent and time of first mobilisation in 36 percent of charts, while rescue antiemetic doses were almost always recorded.
Recorded rescue antiemetic doses agreed well with nurse-assessed clinically important nausea or vomiting (kappa 0.71) in 1,120 day surgery patients.
Surgeon-level intraclass correlation for failure was 0.09 across 31 surgeons after adjustment, partly explained by drain use and review timing.
Eleven of 14 day-case discharge models were at high risk of bias, with a median 6 events per candidate predictor; c statistics fell by 0.05 to 0.11 on validation.
A nurse-led readiness assessment at four hours took a median of 6 minutes, and 88 percent of patients assessed as ready went home the same day.
annotations.limitations: Older study; needed a dedicated nurse the unit could not sustain.

annotations.keyFindings: Patients wanted advance warning of a likely overnight stay; late conversions caused frustration, and patients living alone or far away worried most.

claims.text: In 2,940 elective laparoscopic cholecystectomies, same-day discharge failed in 21 percent, and a nine-predictor model reached a c statistic of 0.72 without validation.
claims.passage: A model with nine predictors had a c statistic of 0.72 in the development data.
claims.interpretation: Booking-time prediction is plausible, but an unvalidated model overstates performance.

claims.text: Nausea severity was documented in 41 percent of charts and the time of first mobilisation in 36 percent.
claims.passage: Nausea severity was documented in 41 percent of charts, and the time of first mobilisation in 36 percent.
claims.interpretation: Charts are a poor source for these two variables.

claims.text: Same-day discharge failed in 38 percent of operations starting after 14:00 and 14 percent of those starting before 11:00.
claims.passage: same-day discharge failed in 38 percent of operations starting after 14:00 and in 14 percent of those starting before 11:00
claims.interpretation: List position is a modifiable predictor and must be handled as such.

claims.text: Eleven of 14 day-case discharge prediction models were at high risk of bias, with a median of 6 events per candidate predictor.
claims.passage: Eleven were at high risk of bias, most often because of too few events for the number of candidate predictors (median 6 events per candidate predictor)
claims.interpretation: Events per candidate predictor and validation decide whether a model is usable.

claims.text: Rescue antiemetic doses in the electronic medication record agreed well with nurse-assessed clinically important nausea or vomiting (kappa 0.71).
claims.passage: Agreement for clinically important nausea or vomiting was good (kappa 0.71).
claims.interpretation: Nausea needing treatment can be measured from existing records.

claims.text: A nurse-led discharge readiness assessment took a median of 6 minutes, and 88 percent of patients assessed as ready went home the same day.
claims.passage: Of patients assessed as ready, 88 percent went home the same day.
claims.interpretation: A prospective readiness assessment gives better variables but needs dedicated nursing time.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Booking-time predictors of failed same-day discharge are plausible (age, anaesthetic risk, rescue-treated nausea, drains, list position), but most published prediction models are at high risk of bias from too few events per candidate predictor and lack validation. Charts document nausea severity and mobilisation poorly, which supports the case for prospective data, yet rescue antiemetic doses in medication records are a validated proxy for nausea needing treatment. List position is strongly associated with failure and is partly chosen by risk, and surgeons cluster. A nurse-led readiness assessment gives good data but needs dedicated nursing time. Patients want advance warning of an overnight stay.
gradeRationale: Observational development studies at risk of bias, one review of models, and validation evidence for one proxy; certainty about which predictors will perform locally is low.
summary: Eight retrieved records appraised; six source-derived claims; certainty low.
